candidates.summary: one flag set serves both subcommands, so `plan` advertises and accepts eight flags it cannot act on (-out, -gnodev, -port, -base-root, -base-url, -pr, -chrome, -timeout)
candidates.failure_scenario: `gnopreview plan -chrome /nonexistent -port 1 -timeout 1s -out /nope -root <tree> -changed /dev/null` prints the plan JSON and exits 0, and `gnopreview plan -h` lists all thirteen flags. A CI author who puts a render flag on the plan step, or misspells a value, gets no error and no screenshots; the flags each subcommand actually reads are only discoverable by reading render().

candidates.summary: gnodev's scratch state is written into -out, the directory that gets published: the keybase at <out>/.gnodev-<port> (177) and the two logs (183), which .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml then has to delete by name before upload
candidates.failure_scenario: pr-preview.yml:103 carries `rm -rf _preview/gnodev.log _preview/gnodev-base.log _preview/.gnodev-*` as the only thing keeping the gnodev home and the logs out of the published static site. The guard is at the caller, in another repository file, against three hardcoded names: a fourth scratch file, a renamed log, or any second caller (a local `gnopreview render` the docstring invites, a future workflow) publishes the keybase directory. The deeper form is a work dir of its own — os.MkdirTemp or a -work flag — so -out holds only what is meant to be served.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'rm -rf _preview' .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml, then grep -n 'cfg.out' misc/gnopreview/main.go to list what render writes there

candidates.summary: the base pass is a hand-copied second instance of the head pass: boot, Crawler literal, waitReady on urlOf(realms[0]), Run, Write appear at 117-140 and again at 252-279, so every fix to the sequence has to be made twice
candidates.failure_scenario: The unguarded urlOf(...Realms[0]) probe already exists at both 131 and 267, and the base copy carries none of the head copy's later steps. A fix applied to render() — a guard on the empty realm list, a second probe, a shorter readiness timeout — silently leaves the base pass on the old shape, and the failure shows up as a missing 'before' image nobody can trace. The deeper form is one function (or a Crawler method) taking root, dirs, realms and prefix, with render() and renderBase() differing only in their arguments.
candidates.verify_by: read main.go:117-140 beside main.go:252-279; both call startGnodev, build a Crawler, call waitReady(base, urlOf(realms[0]), cfg.timeout, died), Run and Write in that order
candidates.evidence: render(): startGnodev 117, Crawler literal 123-130, waitReady 131, c.Run 134, c.Write 138. renderBase(): startGnodev 252, Crawler literal 259-266, waitReady 267, base.Run 271, base.Write 275. Crawler.Seeds() (crawl.go:75-103) already derives urlOf(c.Realms[0]) as its first seed, so both call sites recompute what the crawler owns.

candidates.summary: render() writes its results back into the Plan it was handed (plan.Pairs 149, plan.Shots 151), so one struct is both the plan subcommand's output and the render subcommand's report
candidates.failure_scenario: Plan carries Shots and Pairs (plan.go:84-89) that BuildPlan can never set and that `gnopreview plan` can never emit, and renderBase() takes the same *Plan as read-only input while render() mutates it. A reader of preview.json cannot tell which fields describe the intention and which describe the outcome, and any future caller that plans once and renders twice gets the first render's screenshots in the second's record.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'plan\.\(Shots\|Pairs\)' misc/gnopreview/*.go and grep -n 'Shots\|Pairs' misc/gnopreview/plan.go: the fields are declared on Plan, never written by BuildPlan, and only assigned in render()
candidates.evidence: plan.go:84-89 declares Shots []Shot and Pairs []ShotPair on Plan; BuildPlan (plan.go:193-279) never touches either; main.go:149 and 151 are the only writers, both inside render(), between the two writeJSON calls at 113 and 153
